mgmt_bio.text: He has founded eight billion-dollar or multibillion-dollar companies, six of them publicly traded - United Waste Systems, United Rentals, XPO, GXO Logistics, RXO and QXO - and with his teams has completed roughly 500 mergers and acquisitions and raised more than $60 billion in institutional capital. In April 2025 he closed QXO's roughly $11 billion acquisition of Beacon Roofing Supply. He announced in December 2025 that he would leave his chairman roles at XPO and GXO Logistics at year-end to concentrate on QXO. He is also managing partner of Jacobs Private Equity, LLC.

sentences.quote: He has founded and led eight companies, all of which he grew into billion-dollar or multi-billion-dollar corporations. He has completed approximately 500 M&A transactions and raised $60 billion in institutional capital.
sentences.text: Chairman and chief executive Brad Jacobs brings an unusual dealmaking record, having founded and led eight companies, completing approximately 500 M&A transactions and raising $60 billion in institutional capital, including United Waste, United Rentals and XPO.

The same roll-up playbook has moved fast at QXO: Beacon Roofing Supply for about $11 billion, completed April 2025, Kodiak Building Partners for $2.25 billion on April 1, 2026, and TopBuild for roughly $15 billion on July 1, 2026.

Scale has so far outpaced profit: second-quarter 2026 results showed a diluted loss per share of $(0.14) on net sales of about $3.25 billion, up 70.3%, with about $6.03 billion of long-term debt at June 30, 2026 plus a $3 billion term loan for TopBuild.

sentences.text: QXO, founded by Brad Jacobs, pursues a strategy to create a tech-forward leader in building products distribution through accretive M&A and organic growth, including greenfield openings.

sentences.quote: The $11 billion transaction, valued at $124.35 per share, was finalized on April 29, 2025, with QXO acquiring all outstanding shares through a tender offer and subsequent merger.
sentences.text: The Beacon Roofing Supply acquisition made QXO the largest publicly traded distributor of roofing, waterproofing and complementary building products in North America, closing in April 2025 at a valuation of $10.6 billion.

sentences.quote: Management is pursuing an aggressive consolidation strategy in a fragmented, roughly $800 billion building products distribution market with a stated revenue goal of $50 billion within the next decade.
sentences.text: Management is consolidating a fragmented, roughly $800 billion building products distribution market with a stated revenue goal of $50 billion within the next decade.

sentences.quote: We believe that approximately 30% of the roofing supply industry remains fragmented, held by over 500 dealers that remain locally competitive. We see extensive M&A opportunities in complementary categories, including insulation, siding and waterproofing, among others.
sentences.text: QXO states that about 30% of the roofing supply industry remains fragmented across over 500 dealers, with further M&A opportunity in insulation, siding and waterproofing.
Announced deals include TopBuild for approximately $17 billion and Kodiak Building Partners for $2.25 billion.
